newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Granada to gain from Forte deal.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Granada to gain from Forte deal.

text.p: British media and leisure company Granada Group is expected to post a 100 million stg improvement in pre-tax profit when it reports full-year figures on Wednesday.
The rise will be driven by the contribution from Forte Plc, the family-run hotel and catering empire which Granada acquired for 3.9 billion stg in January after a bitter takeover battle.
Analysts are forecasting pre-tax profit in a range of 451-468 million stg for the year to September 30, against 351.3 million stg a year ago.
Attention has recently focused on the disposal of 17 luxury Forte Exclusive hotels which Granada has put on the market.
Analysts expect the sale to be announced in the next couple of months and to raise 800-950 million stg.
"My understanding is that there are constant negotiations going on concerning different permutations," said one analyst.
"Granada are trying to bundle up the hotels so that they can dispose of some of the less attractive ones in a package with the prime assets," he added.
Granada has made a series of disposals since the acquisition, raising some 400 million stg to cut its debt.
Earlier this month it sold its stake in airlines services group Alpha Airports for 52 million stg.
It also plans to sell 21 Welcome Break UK motorway service areas and its 68 percent stake in Savoy Hotels Plc.
Granada said it could improve profits from Forte by an annual 100 million stg and the market will be seeking an update on its progress.
Granada has begun work on revamping the Little Chef roadside restaurants it acquired in the deal and has also introduced new pricing structures at UK mid-market hotels.
Analysts are divided on the prospects for Granada's Media and Rental and Computer Services division, some suggesting the results from these divisions will be uninspiring.

Granada, which operates the commercial television (ITV) franchises for north-west England and London at weekends, has built up a total stake of some 27 percent in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television and is expected to table a bid for its northern neighbour at some point.

A recent easing of media ownership laws would make such an acquisition possible but analysts believe that Yorkshire's high share price has persuaded Granada to put these ambitions on hold. Yorkshire has a market capitalisation of just over 700 million stg.
Granada shares were 10 1/2p higher at 893 1/2p on Friday lunchtime, just below 1996 highs of 903p.
